title: A Preregistered Paired Evaluation of Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR) for Intent→Configuration NetOps: Null Results on a Synthetic Verifier-Checked Task Bank
abstract: We report a fully preregistered, archived paired experiment that tested whether a deterministic verifier plus a bounded LLM-guided repair loop (Generate–Verify–Repair, GVR) reduces verifier-detected semantic invariant violations for intent→device-configuration translation. The confirmatory design used a public synthetic NetOps task bank (N = 240 paired tasks), gpt-5-mini as the generator, and a pybatfish-style deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Execution used shared-initial-candidate semantics (one generated candidate per task reused across arms) and allowed at most one bounded repair attempt per task. All planned episodes completed (planned_episode_count = 480; completed_episode_count = 480) with model_calls_used = 240 (shared-generation). Every generated candidate satisfied the deterministic verifier in both arms: n11 = 240, n10 = n01 = n00 = 0. The paired estimate (rate_GVR − rate_baseline) = 0.0; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729). Two preregistration/execution issues in the archived artifacts affected interpretation: (1) shared-generation semantics removed per-arm stochasticity assumed by the preregistered power calculation, and (2) the prespecified schema-constrained-baseline comparison (C vs B) was not executed and no rationale appears in the archive. Conservatively interpreted, bounded GVR provided no additional verifier-detectable benefit in this specific artifact-backed setting because no verifier-detectable errors occurred; results do not generalize beyond the executed semantics, model, task bank, repair budget, or verifier.

sections.introduction:
Automating intent→device-configuration translation with large language models (LLMs) promises operational efficiency but raises safety and correctness concerns: stochastic generators can emit syntactically plausible yet semantically incorrect commands that violate network invariants (reachability, required workflow sequences, or ACL/policy predicates). Prior literature therefore recommends interposing deterministic validators and iterative repair (generate–verify–repair, GVR) so mechanically checkable defects are detected and corrected before execution.

We preregistered and executed a confirmatory paired experiment (study c1_gvr_semantic_eval_prereg_v1) to evaluate whether a bounded GVR intervention reduces verifier-detected semantic invariant violations relative to an unconstrained LLM baseline (and, prespecified, relative to a schema-constrained baseline). The experiment used a public synthetic NetOps task bank (240 paired tasks: 12 topology/policy clusters × 20 tasks) and a single generator/prompt pairing (requested model: gpt-5-mini). The deterministic verifier implemented explicit pybatfish-style checks returning structured diagnostics (violation_count and detailed violation lists). The preregistered design, analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1), and execution manifest were frozen prior to observing results and are archived as the authoritative record of this run.

Key high-level findings are simple and artifact-backed: under the executed shared-initial-candidate semantics (one generation per task reused across arms) the shared candidate satisfied the verifier for every task in both arms (n11 = 240); no repairs were applied in the guarded arm; the paired effect estimate is 0.0 with exact McNemar p = 1.00 and paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0]. Two design/execution mismatches that affect interpretation are documented in the archive and discussed below: (a) the preregistered power calculation assumed independent per-condition generation, but the executed shared-generation semantics remove within-pair stochasticity and thereby remove discordance potential; (b) a prespecified comparison (GVR vs schema-constrained decoding) was not executed in the archived run. We present the artifact-grounded results, an evidence-to-claim mapping requested by reviewers, a nearest-work comparison matrix, and concrete reproducible recommendations for follow-up evaluations that restore the preregistered inferential assumptions.
sections.related_work:
Three streams of prior work motivate and contextualize this study. First, empirical and survey literature documents LLM hallucinations and incorrect outputs for code and structured artifacts, motivating deterministic verification in pipelines [10.2139/ssrn.6754899; 10.18653/v1/2024.findings-emnlp.404; 10.1145/3728894]. These studies show that unconstrained generation may produce flawed artifacts that pass superficial checks but fail deeper invariants.

Second, methodological work on generate–verify–repair and constrained decoding reports improved mechanically checkable properties (compilation, syntactic validity, schema compliance) when deterministic validators or grammar constraints are interposed between generation and acceptance [10.26434/chemrxiv.15005091/v1; 10.36227/techrxiv.177219979.94060974/v1]. Such case studies motivate GVR but also underscore that syntactic or executable improvements do not automatically imply domain-level semantic correctness for complex NetOps invariants.

Third, NetOps-specific research emphasizes verifier-driven evaluation (reachability and policy invariants) and intent-based translation systems where domain semantics and workflow policies are central [10.1145/3656296; 10.1145/3718958.3750537]. These systems commonly integrate validators or domain-specific oracles and recommend human oversight for high-stakes changes.

Our run differs from prior work in three principal ways: (1) the experiment was preregistered with a frozen analysis executor and sample plan; (2) it used a paired confirmatory design on a synthetic task bank with explicit deterministic verifier predicates; and (3) it executed under shared-initial-candidate semantics (one generation per task reused across arms), a decisive execution detail that removed within-pair stochastic variation and produced the degenerate null outcome we report.
sections.methodology:
Preregistered question and hypotheses. The preregistered primary research question tested whether bounded GVR (deterministic verifier + at most one bounded LLM repair attempt) reduces verifier-detected semantic invariant violations relative to (A) unconstrained LLM generation and (B) schema-constrained decoding. Confirmatory hypotheses (H1 and H2) and estimands were frozen prior to execution; the primary estimand was the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline computed by paired_binary_analysis_v1. The preregistration specified Bonferroni correction across the two primary comparisons and a fixed-N design (N = 240 paired tasks).

Execution contract and frozen semantics. The archived execution used adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and the requested generator gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json). Crucially, generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (independent_condition_generation = false) and initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1 (bounded single repair). Planned_episode_count = 480 (two conditions × 240 tasks), and the execution manifest reports completed_episode_count = 480 and model_calls_used = 240 (shared-generation reuse). The deterministic verifier was deterministic_netops_validator_v5 with scoring rule full_intent_constraint_validation; the task bank entries include explicit required_sequence and expected_final_state constraints that the verifier checks.

Task bank and oracle. The synthetic NetOps task bank encodes initial device states, intent descriptions, workflow constraints, and expected final states; per-task difficulty metadata and required_sequence fields are archived in execution/task_manifest.jsonl. The deterministic validator executes topology-aware predicate checks (reachability, required command sequence presence, protected-interface preservation) and returns structured diagnostics (violation_count and explicit violations list). Representative per-task validator traces appear in execution/scoring/*.json and execution/responses/*.txt.

Analysis plan and preservations. The preregistered analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1) performed the paired exact McNemar-style test and computed absolute risk reductions with paired-bootstrap CIs (bootstrap_resamples = 10,000; seed = 1729). Missingness rules and conservative sensitivity analyses were preregistered; execution artifacts record zero failed episodes and zero flagged contamination items (analysis/missingness_summary.csv; analysis/contamination_summary.csv). All raw responses, validator traces, and analysis artifacts are archived and referenced below in the evidence-to-claim mapping.
sections.results:
Execution and accounting. The execution manifest reports planned_episode_count = 480, completed_episode_count = 480, failed_episode_count = 0, complete_pair_count = 240, and model_calls_used = 240 (shared-initial-candidate semantics). Deterministic reconciliation artifacts confirm consistency across provider-call accounting and episode totals. Representative response files show that the shared initial candidate was reused as the response in both arms for every pair (examples archived under execution/responses/ and execution/scoring/).

Primary confirmatory outcomes. The analysis executor produced the contingency table: n11 = 240 (both arms accepted), n10 = 0 (guarded only), n01 = 0 (baseline only), n00 = 0 (both rejected). Baseline_success_rate = 1.0; guarded_success_rate = 1.0; paired estimate (rate_GVR − rate_baseline) = 0.0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00. Paired-bootstrap 95% CI (paired_bootstrap_percentile; 10,000 resamples, seed 1729) = [0.0, 0.0]. Analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; analysis/condition_summary.csv; analysis/analysis_log.jsonl) are archived and authoritative for these numbers.

Repair usage and failure modes. For every episode the validator trace records repair_applied = false; the bounded repair loop never executed because the shared initial candidate satisfied all validator predicates across the task set. Thus no repair-iteration distribution exists (empirical survival function degenerate at zero). The contamination and missingness summaries record zero flags and zero infra failures.

Degenerate inference and preregistration mismatch. The observed contingency—zero within-pair discordances—makes the paired comparison degenerate: there is no within-pair information to estimate a differential effect. The archived preregistered power calculation assumed independent per-condition generation; shared-generation semantics violate that assumption and deterministically reduce discordance potential. The manifest documents this design choice and its deterministic effect on the paired analysis.
sections.discussion:
Conservative scientific interpretation. Artifact-grounded and conservatively stated: in the executed setting (single generator/prompt pairing, shared-initial-candidate semantics, synthetic task bank, single bounded repair attempt, deterministic validator implemented invariants), bounded GVR produced no verifier-detectable benefit because there were no verifier-detectable errors to correct. This observation does not imply that GVR is ineffective in general—rather, it highlights that measurable GVR benefit depends on evaluation semantics, generator stochasticity, verifier coverage, repair budget, and task difficulty.

Design lessons for NetOps reliability evaluation. Two concrete evaluation artifacts determine the ability to detect GVR benefits: (1) generation semantics (shared vs independent generation) set the discordance potential between arms; if a study aims to measure GVR’s efficacy at correcting stochastic generator errors, independent per-condition generation must be used to permit within-pair disagreements. (2) verifier completeness and adversarial task selection determine whether the task set produces verifier-detectable failures at all. The preregistration included golden-reference injections and adversarial checks to validate verifier sensitivity; the archived run shows the golden-injection step was not realized in practice for the executed adapter-configured run and is recommended for follow-up.

Operational recommendations grounded in the archive. (1) Re-run the frozen task bank with independent_condition_generation = true (the archived task_manifest and RNG seeds support deterministic reruns) to restore the preregistered power logic. (2) Inject adversarial/golden tasks (the preregistration planned 10% golden tasks) whose verifier label is known to validate oracle sensitivity. (3) Expand generator scope (multi-model runs) and increase repair budget to measure how iterative repair affects correction rates. (4) Broaden verifier coverage (additional semantic invariants or formal/SMT hybrids) to reduce oracle incompleteness risk; the evidence synthesis identifies stronger formal integration as an open gap.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: the preregistered power assumptions assumed independent-generation; executed shared-generation semantics violated this assumption and removed discordance potential. Construct validity: passing the deterministic verifier does not guarantee absence of other operational risks outside the verifier’s encoded invariants. External validity: synthetic tasks, a single model (gpt-5-mini), and a single repair budget limit generalization. Conclusion validity: zero discordant outcomes preclude evidence that GVR changes verifier-detectable rates under the executed semantics. These limitations are summarized in the final limitations list below.
sections.conclusion:
We executed a fully preregistered, artifact-archived paired experiment evaluating bounded GVR for intent→configuration NetOps on a public synthetic task bank. Under the executed shared-generation semantics every generated candidate satisfied the deterministic verifier (n11 = 240), yielding a degenerate null paired estimate (0.0), exact McNemar p = 1.00, and paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0]. Conservatively interpreted, bounded GVR did not add verifier-detectable value in this artifact-grounded setting because no verifier-detectable errors occurred. However, two preregistration/execution deviations constrain inference: (1) shared-generation semantics invalidated the preregistered independent-generation power assumption; and (2) the prespecified schema-constrained-baseline comparison (C vs B) was not executed and the archived artifacts contain no recorded rationale. We release the authoritative archived artifacts so others can reproduce the accounting and extend the evaluation under independent-generation, adversarial/golden injections, multi-model regimes, and expanded verifier coverage to more robustly assess GVR’s operational value.

Evidence-to-claim mapping (concise). The following compact mapping ties principal assertions to archived artifacts (artifact paths are provided; readers may consult the full archived manifests for complete cryptographic indices):

- Claim: All pairs completed and model_calls_used = 240 under shared-generation semantics. Evidence: execution/execution_manifest.json; execution/model_configuration.json; analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json.
- Claim: Every generated candidate passed the deterministic verifier in both arms (n11 = 240). Evidence: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; analysis/condition_summary.csv; execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json (representative traces) in execution/scoring/.
- Claim: No repairs were applied (repair_applied = false for all episodes). Evidence: execution/scoring/*.json verifier_trace.validation_after.repair_applied and analysis/condition_summary.csv.
- Claim: Paired estimate = 0.0; exact McNemar p = 1.00; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0]. Evidence: analysis/results.json and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl.
- Claim: Prespecified schema-constrained comparison (C vs B) was not executed in this archived run. Evidence: preregistration and execution manifest comparisons recorded in execution/execution_manifest.json and preregistration record (preregistration archived alongside execution manifest). 

Nearest-work comparison (compact). Table: each entry gives closest prior study and one-line difference to this run (see cited references):

- NetConfEval (intent→config benchmarking) [10.1145/3656296]: prior benchmark; our contribution = preregistered paired confirmatory test with deterministic verifier and explicit shared-generation semantics.
- MeshAgent / intent-driven NetOps prototypes [10.1145/3771567]: prototype systems integrating LLMs+validators; our contribution = controlled paired experiment with frozen analysis executor and public synthetic tasks.
- GVR/repair methodological case studies [10.2139/ssrn.6754899; 10.36227/techrxiv.177219979.94060974/v1]: prior work shows generate–verify–repair improves mechanically checkable properties; our run provides an artifact-backed null under shared-generation semantics and documents design choices that eliminate discordance potential.

Reproducibility checklist (brief). To deterministically reproduce or extend the run consult these archived inputs: execution/task_manifest.jsonl, execution/model_configuration.json, execution/provider_calls/*, execution/raw_results.jsonl, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, and the preregistration manifest. The archived execution manifest and full hash manifest contain the authoritative indices for all artifacts.

Representative illustrative example. A typical task’s reference and generated configuration (representative files archived under execution/responses/ and execution/scoring/) are: "interface edge1 admin down
interface edge1 vlan 30
interface edge1 mtu 1600
interface edge1 admin up"; the validator traces for that task record violation_count = 0 before and after validation and repair_applied = false.

Overall, the artifact-backed null outcome emphasizes that evaluation semantics and verifier coverage drive measurable evidence of GVR efficacy; future evaluations should restore per-arm stochasticity and adversarial/golden-task injections to test GVR under discordant-generation regimes where repairs are needed and measurable differences can arise.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and verifier scope: N = 240 tasks were synthetic and evaluated against a pybatfish-style deterministic validator; results may not generalize to production topologies, vendor-specific syntax, or semantic invariants not encoded in the verifier.

Shared-generation semantics: the archived run used generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one initial generation per task reused across arms). This design reduced model-call cost but also removed per-arm stochastic variation and therefore reduced sensitivity to detect GVR benefits that rely on independent per-condition generator variability; the preregistered power calculation assumed independent per-condition generation and therefore does not apply to the executed design.
Single-model evaluation: the experiment used one generator (gpt-5-mini); cross-model generality is not established.
Repair budget: only a single bounded repair iteration was permitted; different or larger repair budgets or iterative strategies might produce different outcomes.
Verifier completeness risk: passing the deterministic verifier does not guarantee absence of all operational risks (unobserved invariants or properties outside the verifier model).

Prespecified comparison not executed: the preregistration included a prespecified schema-constrained-baseline comparison (C vs B) that was not executed in the archived run; the artifacts do not record a rationale, which is an unresolved procedural limitation.
